The image does not directly write “mouth” or complete anatomical names, but uses letters to label different positions. Reasoning: The question asks “what is located at the opposite end of the mouth or away from the mouth.” In biological terminology, oral means the mouth part or the side toward the mouth; aboral means away from the mouth, the side opposite the mouth. Therefore, the structure located opposite the mouth or away from the mouth is called the Aboral Pole.
